verdict: Ready for scoped preparation after remaining operational gates
scope: Bounded validation of the privileged mount-helper timeout finding; no whole review rerun or live operation

finding_followup.evidence: docker create cannot start a process; the returned full ID is checked against immutable image, exact name, operation/unit labels and restart=no, then durably recorded in an exclusive fsynced intent before docker start. Start/wait uncertainty checks that same owned ID and kills it if still running. Completion requires wait exit0 and stopped/nonrestarting state. Mount state and workspace preimages are retained; no rm/unmount/retry is introduced.

cases: unacknowledged create remains stopped without start
accepted start timeout retains intent and contains original helper
exit0/stopped helper writes intent/completion and verified bounded-storage receipt
foreign ownership before start refuses without start/kill
ownership drift after start refuses unsafe containment and preserves uncertainty
nonzero mount exit refuses completion receipt

limits: Mocks establish client/daemon outcome ordering and identity refusal, not real Docker/nsenter/mount behavior.
If current identity inspection or Docker containment itself is unavailable, the operation remains uncertain and retained for operator reconciliation; no automatic retry is authorized.
Actual final approval sizes, signatures, Linux oracle controls, source deployment and owned stopped-resource checks remain operator execution gates.
Pricing horizon is planned at12hours and approvals24hours before preparation, never extended during the active campaign.
